limitations: Optional experimental Rust patch; the default vendored source and public library do not apply it.

This slice changes mixed Decimal/FLOAT-or-DOUBLE binary comparisons, including BETWEEN, simple CASE, equal_null and explicit DISTINCT FROM. It does not implement general Spark type coercion or alter ordinary FLOAT/DOUBLE-only comparisons.

The 25 previous numeric corpora retain 180 value/type/coarse-stage differences. The new corpus retains 128 observations: 112 high-scale Decimal-to-DOUBLE rounding observations, eight IN-list coercion observations, four EXISTS and four IN-subquery projection/planning observations. These are observations, not independent bugs.
Five older error-cause gaps, four empty-subquery cause gaps and four wrapped-sort diagnostics remain outside the coarse numeric agreement count.

The shared resolver inspects types for comparisons. Only mixed Decimal/float pairs acquire the Rust normalization UDF and native Decimal-to-DOUBLE cast. FLOAT widening and normalization share one array pass; each operand is evaluated once within a binary comparison.

Decimal-to-DOUBLE continues to use native Arrow CAST, including its known rounding difference around 2^53 for DECIMAL(38,18). The standalone CAST diagnostic reproduces that difference before and after this patch.

The local corpus was designed for these code paths and checked against Spark 4.2.0. It is not a complete Spark or upstream CI compatibility suite; the numeric comparator excludes full schema metadata and structured error conditions.

Timing covers 13 in-memory scenarios on one host/compiler. Delta I/O, predicate pushdown, NULL-heavy comparison throughput, concurrency and large comparison trees are unmeasured. Prior unattributed buffer-policy differences around 0.4%-0.7% remain outside this measurement.
